images.title: How a SoFi referral pays both sides
images.alt: Flow of the SoFi bank referral: a member shares a link, a new customer opens an account and makes a small deposit, then both get a bonus.
images.caption: The new customer's bonus is the smaller one; the member who referred them gets more.
images.note: Check SoFi's official rules for current terms

items.text: A SoFi Checking and Savings account, through that link

images.after: Why a bonus doesn't pay out
images.title: Why a referral bonus gets missed
images.alt: Common reasons a SoFi referral bonus doesn't pay: no referral link, an existing SoFi product, a late or small deposit, or referrer account issues.
images.caption: Nearly every missed bonus traces back to one of these, so check them before you sign up.
images.note: Check SoFi's official rules for current terms

items: Account wasn't opened through a referral link
New customer already had another SoFi product
Deposits fell short or started after the deadline
Account was opened after the promotion period ended
Referrer's account was closed or not in good standing
Referrer had hit SoFi's yearly bonus cap

images.after: Should you open an account just for the bonus?
images.title: Open an account for the bonus?
images.alt: Decision on opening a SoFi account for a referral bonus: open it only if you'd use the account anyway, otherwise skip it.
images.caption: Judge the account itself first; the bonus is a thank-you, not a reason.

data.question: Would you use the account even without the bonus?

branches.result: Compare fees, interest and whether you'd move your paycheck there, then decide.
Skip it. A bonus is a poor reason to add an account you'll never use.
